title: Pathway Rotation: Technical Sales
description: Week 3 is the Technical Sales rotation: participants see the profession behind the skill they have been practicing for two weeks. They study the SDR/BDR, AE, and sales engineering role landscape and how sales teams are measured; apply a discovery framework in a live mock call with an industry practitioner and score their pipeline against qualification criteria; and handle objections while analyzing the personal pipeline as a funnel and presenting findings. Weekly milestone: recorded mock discovery call completed; pipeline review presented.
notes: Weekly milestone: recorded mock discovery call completed; pipeline review presented.
lesson_length: Lab-guide lessons, roughly 1200-1800 words each, supporting a full week of live instructor-led practice
learning_objectives: Distinguish SDR/BDR, AE, and sales engineering roles and how sales teams are measured
Apply a discovery framework in a live mock call and score the pipeline against qualification criteria
Handle objections and analyze the personal pipeline as a funnel

lessons.title: The Sales Role Landscape
objectives: Distinguish SDR/BDR, AE, and sales engineering roles and how sales teams are measured
Relate metrics such as meetings booked and pipeline created to the role that owns them

lessons.title: Discovery & Qualification
objectives: Apply a discovery framework in a live mock call and score the pipeline against qualification criteria
Choose open discovery questions that surface need, authority, and timing

lessons.title: Objections & Pipeline Discipline
objectives: Handle objections and analyze the personal pipeline as a funnel
Present funnel findings with a corrective plan for the weakest conversion stage

sequencing_rationale: Week 3 is the Technical Sales rotation: the profession behind the skill practiced for two weeks. Role landscape first (context), discovery second (the live mock call with a practitioner), objections and funnel discipline third because both apply to the pipeline built so far. Scope assumption: discovery frameworks are taught generically (need, authority, timing) rather than a single branded methodology.
